newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS SEEN UP ON U.S. DATA, PESO STRONG.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS SEEN UP ON U.S. DATA, PESO STRONG.

text.p: Dealers saw stocks opening with strong upside potential on Wednesday in the wake of favorable U.S. long bond reaction to U.S. producer price data.
"It was the long bond that took us down yesterday, but volume was thin so a little buying should take us back up again," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed resistance for the IPC index at 5,055 points, up from Tuesday's close of 5,002.88.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 40/32 in early trade to yield 6.57 percent.
Traders expected the peso to open firm on lower U.S. long bond yields combined with increases in primary Cetes rates at Tuesday night's central bank auction.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.7500/7.7800 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.7730/7.7765 per dollar, compared to Tuesday's close of 7.7840/7.7870.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening down from Tuesday's close of 18.80 percent on a firm peso.
